answer: Latency-shadow admission times each new identity’s first outbound messages against the ocean of established traffic, requiring arrival gaps that match organic diurnal drift. A valid identity must let a quill of signed timing metadata accrue across several quiet hours before its traffic gains weight, so burst-created accounts stall at low priority. Each sybil therefore pays wall-clock delay and idle bandwidth, roughly hours of unused capacity per identity, while the nebula of honest peers keeps steady throughput.
